page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 63.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 7.88 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core scores, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, with read-only small block cached memory reaching 840.48 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 49.49 GB/sec. For language model workloads, text generation with a small 135M model achieves top-tier speeds of 373.98 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for medium 7B models is weak, landing in the bottom 25%.

The c4d-highmem-8 offers a high-density memory configuration relative to its vCPU count, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without demanding massive parallel compute scaling. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware limits its utility for high-throughput local database caching or heavy machine learning training. It is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, and small-scale web serving or database operations.
